primary_title: Microbiota-Dependent Crosstalk Between Macrophages and ILC3 Promotes Intestinal Homeostasis
decision_basis: The reviews identify the Mortha primary showing that microbiota-responsive intestinal macrophages produce IL-1beta, which stimulates Csf2/GM-CSF production by ROR-gamma-t-positive ILC3s.
limitations_preserved: Macrophage-to-ILC3 cytokine-output bridge; preserve microbiota/commensal and mouse intestinal context, IL-1R-MyD88 dependence and Csf2 production semantics, without inventing a transcript-to-protein step or inferring SCI relevance.

primary_title: Microbiota-Dependent Crosstalk Between Macrophages and ILC3 Promotes Intestinal Homeostasis
decision_basis: The reviews identify the Mortha primary showing that exogenous Csf2 restores Il10 expression and IL-10 release in Csf2-deficient intestinal macrophages, linking ILC3-derived GM-CSF to a regulatory macrophage output.
limitations_preserved: Protein-output bridge; preserve exogenous-Csf2 rescue and mouse colonic macrophage context, distinguish IL-10 release from Il10 transcript, and do not infer a unique CSF2 receptor subunit or SCI relevance.

decision_basis: The reviews identify the Mortha primary showing that Csf2 deficiency or ILC3-specific Csf2 loss reduces intestinal Foxp3-positive Treg homeostasis, whereas exogenous Csf2 or Csf2-competent ILC3 reconstitution restores Treg induction and frequency.
limitations_preserved: Two-hop functional bridge through intestinal mononuclear phagocytes; preserve the Csf2-deficient/rescue and ILC3-reconstitution contexts, do not collapse the intermediate macrophage/DC function, and do not infer SCI relevance or terminal-TF effects.
